text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high token usage detected for tenant T-ACME (dedicated pool: pool-eu-04). Rate: +120% over baseline in last 30m. Possible billing impact. Paging oncall

maya: on it. paging derek and alex-billing. assigning incident handler.

derek: I see spike in metrics dashboard, lots of small requests from T-ACME between 12:05-12:30 UTC. latency is normal but tokens counted are large. Sending trace sample.

maya: @derek paste traces here. also @jordan-cs do we have an incoming customer ticket from Acme?

jordan-cs: acme-support pinged at 12:22 complaining about unexpectedly high bill preview; they attached org-level usage csv. says they've only had a small load test.

alex-billing: I'm seeing a ~2.1M token delta between our meter and the tenant's reported call logs for the 12:00-12:30 window. Our meter shows 2.7M tokens, they report ~600k.

ryan-ops: running quick grep on ingest logs. suspicious: lots of repeated client_ids hitting the auth proxy with identical request IDs. possible replay or proxy retry storm. sample from proxy logs:

```
2026-03-15T12:08:04Z proxy-eu-04 INFO req_id=abc123 client=T-ACME req_hash=0x5a3f status=200
2026-03-15T12:08:04Z proxy-eu-04 INFO req_id=abc123-retry client=T-ACME req_hash=0x5a3f status=200
2026-03-15T12:08:04Z proxy-eu-04 INFO req_id=abc123-retry2 client=T-ACME req_hash=0x5a3f status=200
```

alex-billing: that would explain double/triple counting if each retry increments token meter. are retries deduplicated upstream?

derek: runtime should dedupe by request fingerprint if the request reaches the same worker, but with our smart routing the retries may have been routed to different replicas because of transient 503s. checking router logs.

maya: business impact? are any other tenants affected?

alex-billing: no, only pool-eu-04 tenant T-ACME shows this behavior. billing delta currently ~2.1M tokens (~$210 incremental at current rate).

jordan-cs: Acme is a dedicated customer on reserved capacity. we need to avoid auto-invoicing surprises. suggest we put an invoice hold and notify their account owner.

maya: agree. @alex-billing can you apply a temporary manual credit or hold while we investigate? include contact in the notice.

alex-billing: placing billing hold now and emailing Acme billing contact. creating billing-ticket BT-8425 and linking incident. note: hold will prevent auto-charge this cycle but accounting still records the usage.

ryan-ops: router logs show an edge LB health-check flapping 12:06-12:09 triggering client retries. health flaps correlate with increased token ingestion. candidate root cause: flaky health probe causing clients to retry at the proxy level, generating duplicate requests counted separately once they hit different workers.

derek: ops: can we snapshot the relevant KV cache + request fingerprint index for pool-eu-04? need to confirm dedupe state.

ryan-ops: taking snapshot now: `/opt/runtime/snapshots/pool-eu-04/1769004321.snap` (pushed to s3). also temporarily disabling aggressive client-side retries via LB config and enabling ``dedupe_by_global_fingerprint=true`` in router for pool-eu-04. applying change (rolling restart of 3/12 routers).

maya: good. initiate canary change and watch token rate. Derek watch the meter.

derek: patch applied to 3 routers. token ingestion rate dropping immediately. current trend: back to +8% over baseline. still investigating historical double-counting.

alex-billing: since usage already recorded, recommend manual reconciliation for T-ACME: credit tokens that match identical req_hash patterns seen 2+ times. I've exported suspect events and will compute duplicates.

jordan-cs: I'll draft customer note: short explanation, mitigation done, hold applied, we'll reconcile tokens and follow up with adjustment. cc: legal/account manager.

maya: ops, what about tenant isolation? could this have impacted other dedicated pools?

ryan-ops: confirmed no cross-tenant leakage; root cause confined to LB/proxy in pool-eu-04. other pools not showing health flaps.

derek: next steps: 1) finish dedupe verification (DEREK) 2) compute duplicate token set and propose credit (ALEX-BILLING) 3) customer communication (JORDAN-CS) 4) postmortem + infra follow-up on LB health probe config (MAYA/RYAN).

maya: assigning owners in incident tracker. estimated MTTR for full reconciliation: 24h. we will push interim credit within 2 hours.

alex-billing: done. generated credit proposal: ~2.0M tokens (CSV attached in BT-8425). pushing interim 100% hold and provisional credit of $200 to avoid SLA penalty.

jordan-cs: message sent to Acme: "We've applied a temporary billing hold and provisional credit while we finish reconciliation. We've mitigated the root cause and will follow up with final adjustment."

derek: capturing logs for postmortem. saving router and proxy traces to `s3://redwood-incidents/1769004321/`

maya: great work. keeping channel open for any regressions. I'll schedule a 1p follow-up to review the reconciliation numbers.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded from SEV2 to SEV3 at 12:42 UTC after traffic normalization. linked BT-8425, PM assigned: maya.

ryan-ops: note for postmortem: adjust LB health probe thresholds and consider global dedupe guard to prevent cross-replica replays being counted multiple times.

alex-billing: once final reconciliation done I'll close BT-8425 and issue final invoice adjustment.

jordan-cs: closing customer loop after final numbers.

maya: closing internal incident channel in 2h if no further drift. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
